title: Isolation does not need to catch all
hook: A case is isolated halfway through being infectious. Does that do much?

knows: R is the average number of people one case infects
R below 1 makes an outbreak shrink
doesNotKnow: that isolating a case early cuts R in proportion to the infectious days removed

misconception: Isolation only matters if it eventually catches everyone, so isolating late does little.
objective: The learner can explain that in a model with even spread, isolating at the end of day 3 of 6 removes half of each case's spread (R 3 becomes 1.5), and that each day earlier removes another share, with day 2 bringing R to 1.

claims.text: If a case with R0 = 3 is infectious for 6 days and spreads evenly across them, isolating at the end of day d (and stopping all later spread) gives R = 3 x d / 6: day 3 gives 1.5, day 2 gives 1.0, day 1 gives 0.5.
claims.source: Even spread: 0.5 infections per day; R = 0.5 x d. Computed in Demo.tsx (rAt) and node.

claims.text: On the stage, 10 cases make 30 would-be infections, 5 per day; isolating after day 3 leaves 15 of them, after day 2 leaves 10.
claims.source: Arithmetic; same constants draw the stage.

claims.text: The model is a made-up infection with even spread across the infectious days and perfect isolation.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question, on the stage ('Toy: ... spread evenly over 6 infectious days') and in the reveal.

claims.text: Real infectiousness is not even across the infectious period, and some spread can happen before symptoms.
claims.source: Ferretti L. et al. (2020) Quantifying SARS-CoV-2 transmission suggests epidemic control with digital contact tracing. Science 368: eabb6936 (brief flagged: verify before use).

recall.question: In a toy model a case with R0 = 4 spreads evenly over 8 infectious days. If every case is isolated at the end of day 2 and spreads no more, what is R?
recall.why: Two of 8 days are kept, a quarter of the spread: 4 x 2/8 = 1.
